truths.truth: A login naming another host sends that host only the typed pair and, when accepted, replaces the saved record with that host and pair. A save that changes the host without both a username and a password is refused with credentials_required, saves nothing and sends nothing to the new host.
truths.evidence: Code: hqptuner/api/routes/connection.py record_from runs `if host != cfg.hqp_host and not (body.username and body.password): raise refuse(CredentialsRequiredError())` before apply_connection, with the owner sentence verbatim. hqptuner/api/login.py passes only body.username and body.password to check_pair, then calls apply_connection(record(host, body pair)). Tests pass: tests/api/surface/test_connection_host_rule.py 19 passed, which includes 4 cases of test_a_save_changing_the_host_without_both_credentials_is_refused_and_sends_nothing (code, record absent, host unchanged, alias fake 0 requests). tests/api/login/test_login_route.py 20 passed. The login tests use a typed pair equal to the stored pair, so they cannot tell the two apart. A separate spot-check did: stored admin/pw, login to 127.0.0.2 as newu/newpw. Every Authorization at the new host was built from 'newpw' (True) and none from 'pw' (False). The record became {host:127.0.0.2, username:newu, password:newpw}. A later host-changing save with no credentials answered 422 credentials_required.

truths.truth: The hosts a:b, target:9000/path?x= and fe80::1%eth0 are refused at the save and at login with nothing saved. ::1 is accepted, and the 8088 lane requests http://[::1]:8088/...
truths.evidence: hqptuner/conf/httpauth.py check_host checks with ipaddress plus a positive label rule plus an httpx.URL probe. url_host brackets IPv6 for the 4 URL builders (HttpConfigClient, check_pair, fetch_log, Config.hqp_http_base_url). Spot-check: check_host refused all three bad hosts, and url_host(check_host('::1')) gave '[::1]'. Tests pass: test_host_address.py 24 passed; test_ipv6_urls.py 4 passed (config client, pair check, log, about each saw http://[::1]:8088); test_connection_host_rule.py::test_a_save_naming_an_invalid_host_is_refused_and_writes_nothing[3 hosts] and test_a_save_naming_the_ipv6_loopback_stores_it_bare; test_login_host.py 3 passed (no cookie, no record, 0 requests).

truths.truth: With connection.json holding host a:b at start, the app starts, /api/health answers 200, and the SPA shows the Connection panel.
truths.evidence: hqptuner/core/connection.py ConnectionStore.read runs check_host on the stored host, so a bad host raises StoreCorruptError. create_app and _adopt_alias already catch that and start unconfigured. remembered() now reads through held_record, so neither login nor GET /api/connection hits a 500. tests/api/surface/test_startup_bad_host.py 6 passed: health 200, login 200, file still on disk, alias not asked. The panel opening is the JS chain tests/js/store/setup.test.js 'test_a_request_refused_for_want_of_a_login_opens_the_panel' (13/13 pass). One SUMMARY open item is stale: it says GET /api/connection and the login still raise on a corrupt record through remembered(store), but remembered now calls held_record (routes/connection.py:142-151).

truths.truth: Without the image marker, a start with no saved host and an empty /api/discover sweep send no request to the alias. With the marker and no saved host, a start still adopts an answering alias (owner ruling 2026-11-08).
truths.evidence: Dockerfile ENV adds HQPTUNER_IN_IMAGE=1. Config.in_image reads it: spot-check gave False when unset, False for '0', True for '1'. lifespan._adopt_alias returns early when not cfg.in_image. routes/discovery.py passes alias=None outside the image, and engine/discovery.discover skips the probe when alias is None. Tests pass: test_alias_marker.py 3 passed (outside-the-image 0 dials, in-the-image dialed); test_discovery_route.py 3 passed (outside-the-image with a listening alias answers []); test_discovery_network.py::test_a_start_in_the_image_with_no_host_adopts_the_alias_served_in_process and test_container_host_alias.py (in_image=True) cover adoption.

truths.truth: An 8088 response over its path's ceiling is refused. An 8088 or 4321 response still dripping past its total deadline on the test clock is abandoned. After a Connection save, the replaced 8088 client is closed once its in-flight requests finish.
truths.evidence: Code: noanswer.reply_ceiling event hook plus under_total on the injected clock in HttpConfigClient, check_pair, fetch_log and fetch_about. engine/control.py _recv_document has a total deadline. ConnectionManager.holding_http is taken in api/deps (Mgr/HttpMgr) and in run() passes. The http_client setter closes the replaced client at once, or when its last holder ends; _retired is gone. apply_connection sets manager.http_client, which is the save's seam. Tests pass: test_http_ceiling.py 8, test_http_deadline.py 5, test_ungated_reader_bounds.py 6, test_login_pair_check.py 7, test_retired_client_closed.py 5 (idle replace closes at once; held replace closes only after the request; held request finishes with its own client's answer; ten replacements all closed), test_control_stall.py 13 (4321 drip raises ControlTimeoutError). Known limit the owner declined: an open METER SSE tab holds a replaced client (SUMMARY open items).

truths.truth: A discovery reply carrying an XML entity declaration is rejected, and one sweep keeps and dials at most the reply cap however many senders answer.
truths.evidence: hqptuner/engine/discovery.py parse_reply uses defusedxml fromstring and the noqa S314 is gone. ParseError, ValueError and LookupError all become NotXmlError, a NotAReplyError that discover skips. _collect stops at MAX_REPLIES=32 or MAX_BYTES=64 KiB and awaits sleep(0) on every datagram. tests/engine/test_discovery.py 20 passed, including test_a_non_reply_datagram_raises_notareply (entity, x-bogus, shift_jis, idna), test_a_sweep_against_a_flood_of_senders_keeps_and_dials_at_most_the_reply_cap (found == dials == MAX_REPLIES), test_a_sweep_waits_on_the_sleep_it_was_handed_once_per_datagram_it_reads and test_a_sweep_against_large_replies_stops_at_the_byte_cap. Known limit the owner declined: the cap counts unparsed datagrams.
